security_audit.summary: All 42 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, benign local development settings, or standard infrastructure placeholders. One medium-risk supply-chain finding remains: the GitHub Actions template uses mutable action tags, including master, rather than immutable commit SHAs.

remediation.issue: GitHub Actions dependencies use mutable tags and a master branch reference.
remediation.suggestion: Pin every action to a reviewed full commit SHA and update pins through a controlled dependency process.

remediation.issue: The Compose template exposes local database and Redis ports with default development credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Label it development-only and require environment-provided credentials before any shared or production use.

remediation.issue: Deployment templates contain organization-specific placeholder names and endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Replace repository names, domains, image names, and cloud settings before applying templates.

content.value_statement: Deployment teams need consistent patterns for CI/CD, containers, Kubernetes, and cloud infrastructure. This skill provides templates and review guidance for planning these workflows safely.
actual_capabilities: Explains six CI/CD stages from linting through production deployment.
Provides a multi-stage Node.js Dockerfile and local Compose development configuration.
Includes Kubernetes Deployment, Service, Ingress, probe, resource, and security-context examples.
Provides Terraform patterns for an AWS VPC, EKS cluster, remote state, and RDS database.
Includes an ArgoCD Application example and External Secrets integration reference.
Supplies deployment checks and rolling, blue-green, and canary strategy guidance.
limitations: Templates use placeholders and must be adapted to your repository, cloud account, and security policies.
The skill does not execute deployments, provision credentials, or validate live infrastructure.
The GitHub Actions template requires action SHA pinning before production use.
It does not replace organization-specific threat modeling, compliance review, or incident procedures.

use_cases.title: Create a delivery pipeline
use_cases.description: Start a staged CI/CD workflow with linting, tests, scanning, image publishing, and environment deployments.

use_cases.title: Review Kubernetes deployment settings
use_cases.description: Compare a service manifest against secure defaults for probes, resources, and container security context.

use_cases.title: Plan AWS infrastructure
use_cases.description: Use the Terraform example as a starting point for VPC, EKS, state management, and RDS design discussions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a CI/CD plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple CI/CD plan for my Node.js service. Include linting, tests, security scanning, image publishing, and staging deployment. Ask for missing details first.

prompt_templates.title: Containerize an application
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my application requirements and propose a multi-stage Docker build. Include a non-root runtime user, a health check, and the assumptions you made.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Kubernetes manifest
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Kubernetes Deployment and list improvements for security context, probes, resources, secrets, and rollout safety. Do not apply changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a GitOps release flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitOps workflow using ArgoCD for staging and production. Include promotion gates, rollback steps, secret handling, and action dependency pinning.

output_examples.input: Create a release checklist for a Kubernetes service.
output: Pre-deployment: confirm tests, scans, migrations, and rollback ownership.
Deployment: monitor rollout status, readiness probes, and error rates.
Post-deployment: verify metrics, logs, alerts, and customer status communication.

output_examples.input: What should I review before using the Terraform template?
output: Replace state bucket, region, network ranges, resource names, and environment variables.
Confirm module versions, IAM permissions, database backup settings, and deletion protection.
Run plan in an isolated account and obtain peer review before apply.

best_practices: Pin CI action dependencies to reviewed commit SHAs before enabling the workflow.
Store production secrets in a managed secret system and reference them at runtime.
Test rollback procedures and deployment health checks before every production release.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder domains, repository names, credentials, or network ranges into production.
Do not publish container images or deploy production changes without protected environment approval.
Do not use mutable action tags or branches for trusted CI dependencies.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy my application?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates. You must review, adapt, and run deployment tools yourself.

faq.question: Can I use the Compose credentials in production?
faq.answer: No. They are local development defaults. Use unique secrets from a managed secret system in production.

faq.question: Which CI platforms are covered?
faq.answer: The included pipeline is for GitHub Actions. The pipeline stages can be adapted to other CI platforms.

faq.question: Are the Kubernetes manifests production-ready?
faq.answer: They are starting examples. Set image names, domains, resource values, secret names, and policy requirements for your environment.

faq.question: Does the Terraform example create AWS resources?
faq.answer: It is a configuration example. Review provider credentials, modules, costs, and organization policies before running Terraform.

faq.question: How should I secure the GitHub Actions workflow?
faq.answer: Pin actions to full commit SHAs, minimize permissions, protect environments, and review third-party action updates.
